title: A lower bound 1.6855 for the planar centred Hardy-Littlewood maximal constant over squares
abstract:
Let c_d be the weak type (1,1) constant of the centred Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator over axis-parallel cubes in R^d: the least C such that alpha |{Mf > alpha}| <= C ||f||_1 for every integrable f and every level alpha. The value of c_d is unknown for every d >= 2. The previously published lower bound in the plane is c_2 >= 3/4 - sqrt(2)/4 + sqrt(6)/2 = 1.62119..., obtained by Aldaz (2000) from a rectangular lattice of unit Dirac masses; the best known upper bound is c_2 <= 4.
This development proves c_2 >= Phi = 1.68550999335552518..., where Phi = ((77 + 16 sqrt 22)/2 - (8 + sqrt 22 - sqrt(70 + 8 sqrt 22))(11 + sqrt 22 - 2 sqrt 2 - 2 sqrt 11 - sqrt(17 + 4 sqrt 22)))/(26 + 4 sqrt 22) is an algebraic number of degree 16. The extremal configuration found is a lattice with unequal masses: columns at spacing h = (5 + sqrt 22)/6 carrying masses alternating 1 and w = (17 + 4 sqrt 22)/9, rows at spacing h + 1. Its level-one set covers the period cell except four thin slots, and truncating and smearing the lattice gives integrable test functions. The development also proves the classical covering bound c_d <= 2^d in every dimension, and 1.685 < Phi < 1.686.
